FOR ARE COMBS

O.FOREWORD
Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 March 1977, after the draft finalized by the Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 This standard is intended to cover the are combs for determination ol areas from maps and plans. Are comb commonly used in cadastral surveys may vary in design. The most common design of are comb is covered in this standard. Since are combs are used in fps system the nomenclature has been changed to are combs in metric system.

0.1 This Indian

1. SCOPE

1.1 This standard combs. 2. PKINCIPLE

lays down the dimetlsions

and general

requirements

of arc

2.1 The principle is to erect false offset ordinates at regular intervals in the The figure is then considered figure, the area of which is to be calculated. as divided into trapezoidal or rectangular strips of constant width. The area is then cxpresscd by the product of the length of mid-ordinate and the where ,%I is the sum width ( see Fig. 1 ). `l`hen area (A ) of strips-d&z, of the ordinates r?rl, nz2 and m3, etc, measured on the scale given on the comb ( Fig. 2 ) and d is the common width between the offset ordinates or parallel lines. The width cl between parallel lines is some integral number of millimetres depending on the scale of map or plan and is chosen such that the area in ares may be found directly for any given scale. Thus, the total length of mid-ordinates will directly represent the area of the figure. 3. CONSTRUCTION AND MATERIAL

3.1 The are comb shall consist of a rectangular plastic sheet from which a central rectangle has been cut out and threads stretched at equal intervals through holes perfuratcd through the plastic sheet as shown in Fig. 2. The linear scales in ares or hcctarcs as shown in Fig. 2 shall be drawn on plastic The threads shall be located in grooves on the plastic surface or on sheet. the undercut surface so that they are not sub,jected to rubbing when are comb slides on the map.

FIG. I 3.2 The rectangular Aat sheet shall be of transparent or opaque plastic. The recommended plastic materials arc acrylic and rigid polyvinyl chloride. The plastic sheets shall be smooth, even on both sides and free from blisters, porosity and other defects. 3.3 The thickness of material shall bc 2f0.2 mm. shall not

3.4 The threads used on the combs may be of nylon fibres and become lonae. The thickness of threads shall be t.Y25+045 mm.

4.1.1 The size of the centrally cut rectangle (see Fig. 2 ) where the threads are fitted through the holes shall be 12 x 8 cm. 4.2 The size of holes and the width between two consecutive lines shall be 0'7kO.l mm and 4 mm respectively. 5. GRADUATIONS 5.1 All graduations of the scale shall be cut stamped, engraved or printed on the are comb and shall be clear, fine and filled up in the black SO as to ensure good legibility without the use of magnifying glass. 5.2 Width of the scales on the are comb marks as shown in Fig. 2. 6. PROCEDURE shall be 2 mm width graduation nylon thread

FOR USE OF ARE COMB

6.1 The plastic sheet is placed over the area to be measured in such a way, that it lies fuliy between two threads. By progressively stretching a pair of dividers along the midordinates between the threads, tel-minated by the boundary lines of the area to be measured, the area of the plan can be calculated. The sum total of all ordinates as obtained by stretching the dirider is placed on the scale of the area printed on the are comb and the ;trea of plan can be read therefrom in arcs or hectares. An illustrative example showing the determination of area by the use of are comb is given is Appendix A.
No%-If the boundories are curved to such an extetlt that appreciable error is likely to be introduced, then areas nlay be calculated by any other aypropriale method.

7. TOLERANCE 7.1 The tolerance for the engraved scale shall be 50.1 mm per centimetre length for a temperature and humidity change of 40�C and 100 pcrccnt respectively. 8. ACCIJRACY 8.1 The accuracy of are comb for area determination lClO ares on any scale or survey. 9. MARKING 9.1 Each are comb shall he marked mark and the year of manufacture.

The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspectlon, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI marked products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a iicence for the use of the IS1 Ccrtiticntion Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution. 10.
